title: Communications Officer (Social Media)
description:
Communications Officer (Social Media)

Location: Hybrid

Salary: FTE £25,000 to £26,500 per annum

Role Status: 28 to 35 hours per week

Closing Date: 19 Nov 2026

Are you creative, curious and passionate about using social media to make a difference

Meningitis Now is looking for a Communications Officer (Social Media) to join our Communications team and help us reach, engage and inspire audiences across our social media channels. Whether you're a recent graduate or have gained experience through college, volunteering or a junior communications role, we'll support you to develop your skills and grow within the charity.

You'll help bring our work to life online by creating engaging content, sharing powerful stories, supporting campaigns and building meaningful connections with our community.

About the Job

Working closely with colleagues across the charity, you'll help manage our social media channels and create engaging content that raises awareness of meningitis, supports fundraising and showcases the impact of our work. You'll be encouraged to bring fresh ideas, spot new trends and help us reach new audiences through creative digital communications.

Key responsibilities:
- Day-to-day management of Meningitis Now's social media channels, including Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and TikTok.
- Create and schedule engaging social media content, including posts, stories, reels, videos and graphics.
- Manage and moderate online communities, responding to comments and messages in a timely and sensitive way.
- Work with colleagues to promote fundraising activities, awareness campaigns, support services and events.
- Manage paid social media campaigns, working with third-party suppliers where appropriate.
- Monitor social media performance and contribute to reporting and campaign evaluation.
- Keep up to date with social media trends and help identify new opportunities for engagement.
- Support wider communications, marketing and campaign activities when needed.

What We're Looking For

Essential:
- Excellent written communication skills and attention to detail.
- A passion for social media and digital communication.
- Creativity and an eye for engaging content.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks.
- Confidence using major social media platforms.
- Ability to work collaboratively with a wide range of people.
- An understanding of how social media can help organisations build awareness and engagement.

Desirable:
- Experience creating content for social media, whether through work, study, volunteering or personal projects.
- Basic knowledge of design tools such as Canva or Adobe Creative Suite.
- Experience creating short-form video content and reels.
- An interest in the charity sector.

Ready to Apply

Please apply by completing the application form on our HR system - you will be redirected on clicking apply.

Please note that due to using an anonymised recruitment process, only responses to the application questions will be used for shortlisting. If you choose to upload a CV or covering letter, this information won't be seen until after shortlisting has been completed.

Closing date for applications: 9am, Thursday, 19 November 2026

Interviews: Tuesday, 1 December 2026

Note: Meningitis Now reserve the right to close this advert early or extend it depending on the number of sufficient applications received. If you are interested, please apply as soon as possible.

title: Communications Officer (Web and Digital Content)
description:
Communications Officer (Web and Digital Content)

Location: Hybrid

Salary: FTE £25,000 to £26,500 per annum

Role Status: 21 to 28 hours per week

Closing Date: 19 Nov 2026

Are you digitally confident, creative and passionate about producing engaging online content that raises awareness, reaches new audiences and makes a real difference

Meningitis Now is looking for a Communications Officer (Web and Digital Content) to join our Communications team and help maintain and develop our website and digital content. This role would suit someone skilled in generating website copy, content management, accessibility, user experience and digital communications.

You'll play a key role in ensuring our website remains engaging, accessible and up to date, helping people find the support, information and help they need.

About the Job

Working with colleagues across the charity, you'll help create website content, support digital projects and ensure a positive online experience for users. You'll also help create and adapt content from across the charity, turning information into engaging and accessible digital communications.

Key responsibilities:
- Support the day-to-day running and development of the Meningitis Now website.
- Create, edit and publish website content using our content management system.
- Manage website update requests from colleagues across the charity.
- Help ensure website content is accurate, accessible and user-friendly.
- Support website development projects and work with external suppliers when required.
- Work with digital agencies on SEO and Google Grant advertising.
- Monitor website performance and contribute to reporting and continuous improvement.
- Adapt content for digital channels, ensuring consistency across the organisation.
- Support wider communications, marketing and campaign activities when needed.

What We're Looking For

Essential:
- Excellent written communication skills and attention to detail.
- Strong organisation and time-management skills.
- Confidence working with digital systems and online platforms.
- Ability to present information clearly and accurately, with excellent attention to detail.
- Good problem-solving skills and a willingness to learn.
- Ability to work quickly and collaboratively with colleagues across the organisation.

Desirable:
- Experience using a content management system (CMS) such as Wagtail, WordPress or similar.
- An understanding of website accessibility and user experience principles.
- Basic knowledge of SEO.
- Experience updating websites through work, study, volunteering or personal projects.
- An interest in digital communications and the charity sector.
- Experience with health information or PIF tick.

Ready to Apply

title: Digital Communications Executive
description:
Digital Communications Executive

Salary: £32,630 per annum

Contract: 12-month fixed-term

Work Pattern: Full Time, 37.5 hours per week, Monday to Friday

Location: WWT Slimbridge GL2. We support hybrid working.

About The Role

We're looking for a Digital Communications Executive who combines technical know-how with a genuine understanding of people, and who puts their colleagues and supporters at the heart of every decision.

You'll be the go-to person for colleagues across WWT, helping them get the most from our digital tools and supporting them in making our digital channels work as best they can, to help WWT thrive.

Through your work, you'll play a key role in connecting more people with wetlands, inspiring action for nature and helping WWT restore wetlands and unlock their power for people and wildlife.

About You

To be successful in this role, you'll have:
- A desire to help others, with the patience, empathy and good humour to support colleagues and get satisfaction from enabling wider teams to do their best work.
- Excellent written, verbal and visual communication skills, with the ability to listen carefully, ask the right questions, explain technical concepts clearly and confidently support non-technical colleagues in using digital platforms.
- Significant experience in a digital communications, digital marketing or web content role, including planning, building and maintaining content in a content management system.
- Hands-on experience building, testing and sending email campaigns, and using analytics to measure performance and keep improving results.
- Working knowledge of HTML and CSS and image editing software (such as Photoshop), with a solid grasp of SEO, usability and accessible, inclusive web and email content.
- A genuine understanding of supporters, with a track record of putting them first and using insight, feedback and analytics to shape content and journeys that work for real people.
- Experience working with external agencies, suppliers or freelancers to deliver digital projects on time and within budget.
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to balance competing priorities from fundraising, marketing and communications teams and pick up live work quickly.

About Us

We're WWT, and we're on a mission to restore the super-powered ecosystems we call wetlands. There's never been a more important moment for our work, and we've got some phenomenal people on the case.

Whether they're taking a new visitor under their wing, or conducting ground-breaking research further afield, our team are second to none. And there's nothing we love more than watching them soar.

Whatever you do here, you'll be helping to restore wetlands and unlock their power. So, the only question left is, what role will you play?

Why you'll love working at WWT
- Wake up every day knowing your work is helping to restore wetlands, and our world
- Be surrounded and inspired by our team of passionate, dedicated people
- 33 days annual leave (which goes up to 38 days after 5 years of service) - this includes bank holidays and you have flexibility to take those days whenever you want
- Free entry to all our wetland centres, including your family
- Free car parking and secure bike storage areas
- Colleague discount on shopping and memberships
- Cycle to work scheme
- Contributory pension scheme
- Life Assurance of three times your salary, for peace of mind for your loved ones
- Independent personal, workplace and financial advice from Care first

Additional Information

This is a full time, 12-month fixed-term contract working 37.5 hours per week, Monday-Friday. Based at WWT Slimbridge Wetland Centre, with the opportunity for hybrid working. The role will be required to be at Slimbridge at least once a week and as required for key meetings.

Closing Date: Monday 30th November 2026

N.B. We reserve the right to close the advert early if we receive a sufficient number of applications from candidates who meet the required skills and experience. We therefore encourage early applications.

Interested?

If you would like to find out more, please click the apply button. You will be directed to our website to complete your application for this position.

WWT is an equal opportunities employer and all applications will be considered solely on merit.

No agencies please.

title: Digital Marketing Executive
description:
Digital Marketing Executive

Cheltenham

Full-Time

£30,000 per annum

Juice Recruitment is delighted to be supporting a highly successful and rapidly growing British luxury fashion brand in their search for a Digital Marketing Executive (Email & SMS). This is an exciting opportunity to join an award-winning business with a strong heritage, exceptional customer following, and ambitious growth plans.

Working within a dynamic marketing team, you'll take ownership of the company's email and SMS marketing activity, helping to drive customer engagement, retention, and commercial performance through well-executed campaigns and customer journeys.

The Role

As Digital Marketing Executive, you will be responsible for the day-to-day management of email and SMS marketing activity, ensuring campaigns are engaging, targeted, and aligned with wider business objectives.

Key responsibilities include:
- Managing email marketing campaigns, automated flows, and audience segmentation through Klaviyo.
- Overseeing SMS marketing activity to ensure communications are timely, relevant, and brand-aligned.
- Acting as the key point of contact for external marketing agencies, ensuring projects are delivered on time and to a high standard.
- Delivering customer loyalty communications across email and SMS channels.
- Planning campaigns around seasonal activity, product launches, key trading periods, and commercial priorities.
- Monitoring and analysing campaign performance, providing regular reporting and actionable insights.
- Collaborating closely with ecommerce, marketing, creative, and customer engagement teams.
- Supporting the ongoing development of customer retention and loyalty initiatives.

About You

We're looking for a commercially-minded and highly organised marketing professional who enjoys balancing creativity with data-driven decision making.

You will ideally have:
- Previous experience managing email marketing campaigns, preferably within Klaviyo.
- Experience working with external agencies and managing stakeholder relationships.
- Strong written communication skills and exceptional attention to detail.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple campaigns simultaneously.
- A genuine interest in customer retention, CRM, and loyalty marketing.
- A collaborative approach and the ability to work effectively across departments.
- Experience with SMS marketing platforms and loyalty programmes would be advantageous.

What's in It for You?

Our client offers an excellent working environment and a comprehensive benefits package, including:
- £30,000 per annum
- 25 days holiday plus bank holidays
- Additional birthday leave
- Enhanced maternity and paternity pay
- Increased benefits linked to length of service
- Generous staff discount
- Cycle to Work Scheme
- Employee Assistance Programme
- Regular workplace perks and wellbeing initiatives

Interested?

If you're passionate about digital marketing, customer engagement, and creating impactful campaigns that drive results, we'd love to hear from you.

INDS

title: Men's Engagement Lead
description:
Men's Engagement Lead

Location: Hybrid (Home or office based, with some required travel to Stroud, Gloucestershire)

Salary: FTE £26,500 to £29,000 (£14.56 to £15.93 per hour)

Role Status: 21 hours per week

Closing Date: 30 Nov 2026

We are looking for a Men's Engagement Lead to help shape meaningful, inclusive support and engagement opportunities for men affected by meningitis.

About the job

As a centre of expertise in meningitis aftercare and support, Meningitis Now delivers specialist, impactful services across the UK through its established Community Support Team. Building on this strong foundation, this new role will develop tailored, inclusive support for men affected by meningitis.

Shaped by men s lived experience, this new role will create new ways for men to connect, remove barriers to support, and embed best practice in engagement with men across the charity.

The role will:
- Co-design and lead evidence-informed support with men who have lived experience of meningitis, creating meaningful opportunities for connection through peer support, events, online groups and tailored resources
- Provide compassionate one-to-one emotional and practical support, manage an active caseload and develop support plans that reflect each individual s needs
- Help men access Meningitis Now s wider services and trusted specialist organisations, and advocate for greater understanding of the lasting effects of meningitis in settings such as education and employment
- Build relationships with men s groups, mental health services, professionals and community partners to raise awareness, encourage referrals and connect men with additional support
- Champion authentic representation and best practice in male engagement across the charity, using learning, feedback and impact measures to improve services and increase male participation
- Work collaboratively across the charity, maintain accurate and confidential records, and follow safeguarding and organisational procedures

The role would suit someone who brings:
- Experience of providing support in a community, health, social care, education, voluntary-sector or similar setting, particularly with people affected by illness, bereavement, trauma, grief or disability
- An understanding of how men may experience and access support, and the ability to adapt services to individual needs
- Strong listening, empathy, communication and relationship-building skills, with the confidence to work with individuals, families, professionals and partner organisations
- Good organisation, digital and record-keeping skills, with the ability to manage priorities, work independently and contribute positively to a team
- A sound understanding of safeguarding, confidentiality and safe working practice, together with a commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion and belonging
- Flexibility to travel and occasionally work evenings or weekends, with reasonable notice. A full driving licence is required

What we're looking for

Essential skills and experience
- Demonstrable experience of how men may experience and access support in relation to bereavement, trauma, grief, disability and medical trauma, and how support may need to be adapted to meet individual needs
- Strong listening, empathy and communication skills, with the ability to respond sensitively and effectively to a diverse range of individuals, families, professionals and organisations
- Confident IT and digital skills, including Microsoft Office, CRM or case management systems, social media and digital platforms used to deliver or administer support
- Strong relationship management and service delivery experience, with the ability to build trust, work diplomatically and maintain confidentiality
- Ability to self-motivate and work on own initiative with strong understanding of safe working practices
- Strong interpersonal skills
- Excellent organisation, administrative and prioritising skills, with the ability to work to multiple deadlines
- Robust understanding of safeguarding practice when working with adults and children at risk

Desirable Selection Criteria
- A relevant qualification at level 3, or equivalent experience gained through paid or voluntary work
- Experience in the charity sector, community or project development
- Experience of public speaking
- Experience of CRM systems
- Experience of moderating online peer-support forums
- Awareness of the issues facing people affected by meningitis

We particularly welcome applications from men, who are currently underrepresented among the users of our services. We are seeking someone with a strong understanding of the barriers men may face in seeking support and an ability to build engagement with men affected by meningitis.

Ready to Apply

Please apply by completing the application form on our HR system you will be redirected on clicking apply.

Please note that due to using an anonymised recruitment process, only responses to the application questions will be used for shortlisting. If you choose to upload a CV or covering letter, this information won't be seen until after shortlisting has been completed.

Closing date for applications: 9am Monday 30 November

Interviews: Tuesday 8 December and Thursday 10 December

Note: Meningitis Now reserve the right to close this advert early or extend it depending on the number of sufficient applications received. If you are interested, please apply as soon as possible.

title: PR Account Manager - inhouse or agency welcome!
company: Moxie and Mettle Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
PR Account Manager

We are looking for a PR Account Manager to join an established communications agency, working across a varied portfolio of clients and sectors.

Our lovely client is happy to look at somebody who works clientside in PR/comms as well as an agency, though you will need to have worked on multiple campaigns at one time and also have been involved with budget planning, as this is a crucial part of the PR account management role.

About You

Some previous PR/communications experience is essential, from agency OR clientside.
- Involvement with budget allocation and planning
- Ability to handle multiple campaigns at one time
- Obviously excellent written communication skills
- The ability to turn complex information into clear, engaging stories
- Ambition and drive to progress your PR career!

The Opportunity

You're rejoining an incredibly collaborative and supportive team whether there is an outstanding culture with clear path for progression and development within the next 12 to 18 months.

You'll be office based three times a week, but the other two days can be remote, and you will also benefit from flexible start times, so for example, your working pattern could 8am-4pm or 10am-6pm or anything in between those hours - which makes your work/life balance a lot easier!

The Role

As an Account Manager, you will take responsibility for managing client accounts and delivering effective communications activity that supports their wider business objectives.

You will work closely with clients to understand their priorities, develop creative ideas and identify opportunities to raise their profile with relevant audiences.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Managing day-to-day relationships with a portfolio of clients.
- Developing and delivering integrated PR and communications campaigns.
- Providing strategic communications advice and recommendations.
- Identifying compelling stories, angles and opportunities for clients.
- Building relationships with journalists and securing relevant media coverage.
- Writing and editing press releases, features, articles, case studies and other content.
- Supporting digital and social media activity where appropriate.
- Managing multiple projects, deadlines and budgets.
- Briefing and supporting junior members of the team.
- Monitoring campaign results and reporting back to clients.
- Keeping up to date with news, media trends and developments relevant to clients.
